targetName: HabitGame Robot Family v18 — production reconstruction and build-modal launch gate

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: V14 beauty and silhouette captures share the explicit render-profile-v14 contract. The camera is fixed before geometry fitting and the floor reflection is excluded from the object mask.

formLanguage: concentric mechanical joints and embedded sockets
warm white enamel with role-coded gold, cyan, and mint accents
closed top, rear, profile, and underside construction
structureKind: heavy load-bearing shell with two main arms and two dorsal manipulators
manager pear shell with transparent brain dome and communication fins
half-scale mini maker shell with two precision arms and artist tray
shared hover-reactor and add-on socket language
motionPotential: blink gaze and five-emotion face animation
heavy two-hand lift and dorsal tool work
manager directing inspecting and brain-state signalling
mini painting tool-use and tray interaction
cloud-covered relocation around a building target
objectClass.notes: The family is reconstructed from role-specific turnaround sheets plus the original three-character concept. Cross-view closure and usable construction motion take priority over inconsistent generated micro-details.

reasoning: Three distinct characters must remain readable simultaneously at build-modal scale.
Every visible arm, hand, dorsal linkage, tray, pointer, dome, fin, and hover assembly requires a semantic pivot and attachment contract.
The family must survive front, profile, rear, top, and underside inspection rather than a single hero angle.
The production version must preserve facial and construction animation while reducing current crew draw-call pressure.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Each role is a mechanical character with a different silhouette, tool grammar, and animation duty; a shared sphere blockout is insufficient.

proportions.note: Non-humanoid hover characters use the armored shell as one head-unit body; articulated arms are specified through attachment contracts.

anatomy.pose: Neutral hover with role-specific arm rest positions, unobstructed visor, and all appendage roots embedded in the shell.

faceLandmarks.note: Normalized within each black-glass visor; no anatomical nose geometry is present.

definitionOfDone: All three roles pass silhouette, attachment, closure, face-animation, tool-contact, material, performance, and build-modal composition gates.
Heavy, Manager, and Mini each remain recognisable from every required turnaround angle without relying on labels.
The real build modal shows all three robots performing simultaneous but non-colliding construction actions around the selected building.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Animated optical face system
qualityCriteria: The visor is a closed curved superellipse aperture nested inside a real metal lip and restrained inner edge light.
Both eyes preserve ring, iris, and highlight depth through blink, gaze, and emotion changes; the mouth follows visor curvature without clipping.
Reduced-motion idle remains perfectly stable with no frame-to-frame positional noise.
failureModes: face reads as flat decals on a black plate
eyes or mouth float beyond the visor at oblique angles
idle animation appears as vibration

featureGroups.name: Transparent dome and animated brain system
qualityCriteria: The dome has clear thickness cues, a lower cyan refraction band, and a warm moving key highlight while keeping internal structures legible.
Brain lobes occupy a layered volume rather than one luminous blob and remain dim enough to preserve internal depth.
The dome cradle and rear hinge/spine read as a plausible removable assembly from side and rear views.
failureModes: brain emission washes the dome into a cyan bubble
dome appears as a solid opaque cap
cradle or hinge floats away from the shell

featureGroups.name: Coherent rear and hover underbody
qualityCriteria: Rear panel seams form intentional closed or terminating paths around the energy/service port.
The service port has at least three nested depth levels and a protected emissive center.
The hover underside uses concentric baffles, repeated radial vents, a dark cavity, and a luminous core with no view-dependent gaps.
failureModes: rear is an unbroken blank shell
service details look pasted on
low-angle view exposes disconnected rings or open geometry

visualDeltaChecks: front pear-shell silhouette, visor width, dome height, and fin span delta
side-view dome cradle, visor projection, fin-root embed, and lower-shell taper delta
rear service-port hierarchy, panel-flow, and symmetry delta
low-angle hover baffle, vent distribution, cavity depth, and core protection delta
eye-ring depth, highlight placement, mouth seating, and animated containment delta
painted composite, brushed metal, visor glass, dome transmission, and emissive balance delta
frame-to-frame reduced-motion stability and absence of z-fighting
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
mustNotDo: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.

Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not pass a role from the family concept alone when a role-specific turnaround exists.
Do not call the result 10/10 without multi-angle evidence, animated face evidence, measured live-scene performance, and real modal proof.
Do not trade away semantic pivots or tool contact just to reduce draw calls.

closed front, profile, rear, top, and underside construction
deep integrated visors and role-specific animated faces
Heavy broad shoulder bridge, layered forearms, four-digit grippers, and twin dorsal arms
Manager low pear shell, oversized circular-eyed visor, transparent brain dome, and swept communication fins

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Manager pear shell and brain-dome identity

nextRequiredEvidence: The v14 front silhouette and animated face remain visually stable while topology changes are made elsewhere.
The hover is one rotationally coherent lenticular crescent embedded into the lower shell, without a detached puck profile from either side or rear.
The brain reads as a luminous nested volume from front, both profiles, rear, and top rather than as front-facing plates.
Each communication fin has a dark embedded root collar, a thick translucent shell, and an internal cyan cavity that remains connected through the full turntable.
Front, front-right, right, rear-right, rear, rear-left, left, and front-left captures are non-degenerate and preserve attachment continuity.
Top and underside captures show a closed dome footprint, symmetric fins, a coherent underbody emitter, and no floating or intersecting service parts.
Reduced-motion retains zero hover bob and camera drift; face blink, gaze, five emotions, and four brain states remain animated.
High and Phone budgets, construction theatre, sockets, Heavy lift, and Mini paint remain regression-safe.
browser render screenshot from your agent's browser/screenshot tool
single side-by-side full reference/render comparison sheet
all critical semantic feature scores at or above their thresholds
self-correction review appended with action=continue before the next pass

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The admitted source is a baked-lighting concept render; sampled palette and response class are usable, but inferred PBR maps are not implementation-authoritative.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The original family concept sets role hierarchy and relative scale.
The Heavy, Manager, and Mini turnaround sheets override the family concept for role-specific shape and closure.
The Mini remains exactly 0.50 of Manager family scale and reads younger through proportion rather than missing detail.
Face graphics remain real animated geometry with blink, gaze, and emotion controls.
Construction choreography is deterministic, respects reduced motion, and is anchored to measured building bounds.
No projected texture is required; identity is reconstructed with procedural geometry and shared PBR materials.

coordinateFrame.front: positive Z points toward the viewer
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: project manager authored envelope = 1.0 family unit; mini root = 0.50

silhouette.boundingShape: Three hovering ovoid robots: wide heavy worker, centered domed manager, compact half-scale mini artist.
silhouette.symmetry: Bilateral chassis symmetry with intentionally asymmetric held tools.

observations: unseen region; symmetric panel continuation only

buildPasses.goal: Lock the three reference-specific silhouettes and closures before local detail: Heavy armored load frame, Manager low pear coordinator, and exact half-scale Mini maker.
acceptance: Heavy reads broad, dense, and load-bearing with forearms and hands dominating its lower silhouette.
Manager reads low and friendly with a large face, clear brain dome, swept fins, and integrated underbody crescent.
Mini reads exactly half-scale, compact and cute while retaining credible precision arms, tray, brush, rear cassette, and mint reactor.
All role attachments begin at named embedded sockets and remain coherent in the eight-angle orbit plus top and underside.
Reduced-motion idle is transform-stable with no visible vibration.

buildPasses.goal: Add visors, shells, articulated parts, role tools and sockets.
acceptance: All observed macro and meso components exist as named pivots.

buildPasses.goal: Wire independent enamel, glass, metal and emissive responses.
acceptance: Materials remain readable under neutral and grazing light.
No source lighting is baked into albedo.

buildPasses.goal: Match bright workshop presentation while preserving neutral inspection.
acceptance: Key, fill, rim, exposure, tone mapping and contact shadows are explicit.

buildPasses.goal: Verify motions, sockets, add-on swaps, picking and exploded view.
acceptance: All robots are explodable and clickable.
Add-ons attach to named sockets and animate from semantic pivots.

buildPasses.goal: Meet high and low phone budgets.
acceptance: High <= 90k visible triangles and <= 95 draw calls.
Low <= 40k visible triangles and <= 60 draw calls.

lodPlan.notes: Phone gameplay and wider family view.

lightingFromPhoto: Large cool-white key light from upper front-left; intensity selected for enamel highlight readability.
Soft blue fill from front-right plus cyan underbody practical lights.
Broad cool rim/environment reflection from overhead lab rings; ACES tone mapping at exposure 1.05.
Viewport-anchored ground plane receives soft contact shadows beneath each hover core.
proceduralStrategy: Generate continuous ovoid chassis and curved visors from scaled sphere/lathe geometry.
Generate every articulated limb and add-on beneath a named pivot group rooted at its socket.
Share a role-parametric factory, material registry, joint-ring system and socket standard.
Expose named parts, sockets, colliders, destruction groups, animation controls and exploded transforms through root.userData.sculptRuntime.
Provide high and low segment-count routes without changing role proportions.
Drive construction presentation from phase/progress/sequence inputs without reading or writing gameplay state.
Merge each procedural tool into one vertex-coloured mesh and instance repeated materials, clouds, dust and sparks.
Anchor the theatre to the live landmark world transform; BuildModalV2 remains a transparent control overlay with no second canvas.
Use deterministic seeded orbit lanes and clear the cloud layer before canonical level review.
